title: Upward Technologies vs OutSystems
content_html:
Upward Technologies vs OutSystems

The choice in Upward Technologies vs OutSystems comes down to who does the building. OutSystems is an AI-powered low-code platform where teams visually build apps and AI agents and connect them to existing systems. Upward Technologies is a Dutch company that builds custom software, integrations and AI agents for you and can also host and run them.

Pick OutSystems if your team wants one platform to build, connect and govern many apps and agents itself. Pick Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) if you want a supplier to study one problem first, then build the software or agent and, if you want, run it for you.

What OutSystems is good at

OutSystems is a platform that teams build on. The points below come from its website, read in November 2026.

  • Visual building of apps and agents. According to its website, OutSystems is "an AI-powered low-code platform to visually develop custom apps and AI agents and integrate with existing systems."
  • Governing agents, not just building them. Its platform page says it is for building, orchestrating and governing AI agents, apps and workflows. It also says you can swap AI models with Amazon Bedrock.
  • A wide range of connections. According to its website, the platform offers a large number of connectors, plus APIs (application programming interfaces) and other connection methods. It says it integrates with core systems, ERPs and CRMs, and it lists Salesforce integration and SAP among its core systems use cases.
  • Choice over where things run. Its website says the platform supports hybrid and sovereign cloud. It also says customers can choose where AI systems run and where data is stored to meet sovereignty requirements.
  • Hosting built for uptime. It offers a cloud product called OutSystems Developer Cloud (ODC). Its security page mentions failover across multiple availability zones.
  • Large, regulated organisations. OutSystems says regulated enterprises use it to modernise legacy systems and run custom apps and agents. It also says it is for building apps and AI agents for mission-critical core functions.

If you want one platform to build many applications, connect them to SAP or Salesforce, and control where they run, OutSystems is built for exactly that.

What Upward Technologies does differently

Upward Technologies is a small software company in Breda. It is not a platform you build on yourself. It builds the software for you.

  • One team builds, hosts and runs. The same team that builds the software can host and run it. Its hosting includes backups, monitoring and a named owner.
  • A paid scoping phase comes first. Every project starts with a three-week paid scoping phase before any code is written. It ends with a go or no-go decision and a document the client could take to another supplier. It does not produce a prototype or a working agent. "Wrong supplier" is an accepted outcome, and Upward Technologies says so in the first week. If you want to know what that document should hold, read what a supplier-neutral scoping document should contain.
  • AI agents for repetitive work. Upward Technologies builds AI agents and automated workflows for work such as processing documents, answering questions, and collecting and preparing data. People keep the decisions that need judgement.
  • A default rule for AI and your data. Its general terms (Article 10) say personal and production data are not sent to third-party AI services. AI work on that data uses local or self-hosted models, unless agreed otherwise in writing.
  • Ready-made products. Next to custom work, it sells separate products that you can use on their own: Bookwise (bookkeeping for Dutch BV groups), Reach (B2B outreach), DocSign (e-signature), Transfer (secure file transfer), Assure (ISO 27001 document control, in beta) and GTM (AI go-to-market software that drafts posts, articles and news for a person to approve). ISO 27001 is the standard for information security management.
  • It runs on its own work. Numerous internal tools and agents run the company's own work.

Upward Technologies is also building ERIS (Enterprise Resource & Intelligence System). This is one business system with AI across it, made to run on the customer's own hardware with local AI models. ERIS is not available yet. The beta with design partners starts in November 2026 and the release is planned for January 2027. Design partner sign-up is at https://upwardtech.nl/en/products/eris#join-design-partner. Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU server, and that has its own costs. See what to budget for on-premise language models.

Which one should you pick

You have developers and many apps to build. Pick OutSystems. A platform with visual tools, a large set of connectors and agent governance suits a team that wants to build and change many applications itself. This is even more true if you already work with SAP or Salesforce.

You already run OutSystems. Keep building there. Adding a second way of building for the same kind of app makes things harder, not easier.

You want one problem solved and someone to run it. Pick Upward Technologies. This fits when an operations, finance or IT lead wants a supplier to scope the work, build the software or AI agent, connect it to the ERP or CRM, and look after it. The paid scoping phase tells you early whether it is worth building at all. For a wider view of the market, see how to choose custom software development.

Your need matches a ready-made product. If the need is e-signature, secure file transfer or bookkeeping for a BV group, a standalone product may be enough. That could be one from Upward Technologies or from another vendor.

FAQ

Upward Technologies vs OutSystems: what is the main difference?

OutSystems is a low-code platform that teams use to build apps and AI agents themselves. Upward Technologies is a software company that builds custom software and AI agents for you after a three-week paid scoping phase, and can also host and run them.

How do LLMs access up-to-date company information?

An LLM (large language model) does not know your current data by itself. It needs a connection to the systems where that data lives, such as your ERP or CRM, so it can read and search the latest records when someone asks a question. The article on letting AI answer from live business data explains this in more detail.

How can AI answer questions using live company data?

The AI has to read from the source systems directly instead of from old exports. OutSystems says on its website that it integrates with core systems, ERPs and CRMs, and Upward Technologies builds integrations and AI agents for the same purpose. Whichever you choose, check where the AI processes your data and read the vendor's terms on it.
